es: Analizar un texto de opinión breve identificando su tesis, su tono y dos recursos de cautela o persuasión, apoyándote en evidencias del texto.

teaching.en: My thesis is simple: our town needs more bike lanes.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es sencilla: nuestra ciudad necesita más ciclovías.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende; suele aparecer al principio con I believe, I will argue o My thesis is.
teaching.audioText: My thesis is simple: our town needs more bike lanes.

teaching.en: Safe lanes may encourage more families to cycle to school.
teaching.es: Unas ciclovías seguras pueden animar a más familias a ir en bici a la escuela.
teaching.explanationEs: May suaviza la afirmación: es un recurso de cautela.
teaching.audioText: Safe lanes may encourage more families to cycle to school.

teaching.en: Surely nobody wants children to cycle in heavy traffic?
teaching.es: Seguramente nadie quiere que los niños vayan en bici con mucho tráfico, ¿no?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica con surely: no espera respuesta, da por obvia la idea del autor y persuade.
teaching.audioText: Surely nobody wants children to cycle in heavy traffic?

teaching.en: In cities with bike lanes, accidents fell by a third, so such plans deserve support.
teaching.es: En las ciudades con ciclovías, los accidentes bajaron un tercio, así que esos planes merecen apoyo.
teaching.explanationEs: Un dato concreto (a third) es una prueba que apoya la tesis.
segments: In cities with bike lanes, accidents fell by
a third, so such plans deserve support.
teaching.audioText: In cities with bike lanes, accidents fell by a third, so such plans deserve support.

teaching.en: Critics argue that lanes are expensive; however, doing nothing costs more.
teaching.es: Los críticos sostienen que las ciclovías son caras; sin embargo, no hacer nada cuesta más.
teaching.explanationEs: Concesión y contraste: el autor cita la objeción y la responde con however.
segments: Critics argue that lanes are expensive;
teaching.audioText: Critics argue that lanes are expensive; however, doing nothing costs more.

teaching.en: The tone is firm but fair, because the writer admits the cost.
teaching.es: El tono es firme pero justo, porque el autor admite el costo.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono se deduce de las palabras: firme en la tesis, justo al reconocer la objeción.
segments: The tone is firm but fair,
because the writer admits the cost.
teaching.audioText: The tone is firm but fair, because the writer admits the cost.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis del autor.

choices.text: The library should stay open until eight.
The library should close earlier to save money.
The library should sell more books.

feedback.es: La tesis aparece al principio: «I believe it should stay open until eight»; el resto la apoya.

hint.es: La tesis suele aparecer al principio, tras I believe.

origin.text: Our library closes at five, just when most people finish work. I believe it should stay open until eight. Some people may say that this would cost too much. However, the library already pays for heating and lights, so a few more hours would add little. Students also need a quiet place to study after school, and many homes are too small or too noisy. Parents who work all day could finally take their children to choose a book. Surely a town that loves books should let its people read them? Last year, the city of Redford opened its library in the evening, and visits rose by a third. I am not saying that every problem will disappear. Even so, the evidence suggests that longer hours would help families, students and workers.

prompt.es: Elige qué recurso es «Surely a town that loves books should let its people read them?».

choices.text: A statistic from a survey.
A rhetorical question that persuades.
A softener with may.

feedback.es: La pregunta no espera respuesta: da por obvio lo que el autor defiende. Es una pregunta retórica.

hint.es: Es una pregunta cuya respuesta el autor da por obvia.

prompt.es: Completa: «Este plan podría ayudar a muchas familias.»

feedback.es: May (o might, could) es un modal de posibilidad que suaviza la afirmación: el plan «podría» ayudar, no se asegura.

hint.es: Es un verbo modal de posibilidad.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué prueba usa el autor para apoyar su tesis?

choices.text: Everyone in town wants longer hours.
Books are cheaper in the evening.
Visits rose by a third in Redford.

feedback.es: Visits rose by a third en Redford es un dato concreto que respalda la idea de abrir más horas.

origin.text: Our library closes at five, just when most people finish work. I believe it should stay open until eight. Some people may say that this would cost too much. However, the library already pays for heating and lights, so a few more hours would add little. Students also need a quiet place to study after school, and many homes are too small or too noisy. Parents who work all day could finally take their children to choose a book. Surely a town that loves books should let its people read them? Last year, the city of Redford opened its library in the evening, and visits rose by a third. I am not saying that every problem will disappear. Even so, the evidence suggests that longer hours would help families, students and workers.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige el tono del hablante.

choices.text: Firm but fair.
Angry and rude.
Unsure and confused.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción (understand the worry) pero mantiene su opinión con firmeza: tono firme pero justo.

origin.audio: I understand the worry about cost, but I'm firmly convinced that the plan is worth it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso que usa el autor.

pairs: Some people may say it costs too much.
The evidence suggests it would help.

feedback.es: Surely…? es una pregunta retórica, some people may say concede una objeción, rose by a third es un dato y suggests es cautela.

pairs: Some people may say it costs too much.
The evidence suggests it would help.

prompt.es: Lee el segundo texto y elige la tesis del autor.

choices.text: Phones should be banned in class.
Banning phones at lunch is a mistake.
Students should talk less at lunch.

feedback.es: «In my view, this is a mistake» declara la tesis: prohibir los celulares en el almuerzo es un error.

origin.text: Many schools now ask students to leave their phones in a locker during lunch. In my view, this is a mistake. It is true that phones can distract us in class. Nevertheless, lunch is our free time, and a rule like this treats teenagers like small children. A survey in one school found that students talked more when phones were allowed, which may suggest that the real problem is not the phone. Some teachers say that phones make the room quieter, but I wonder whether silence is really the goal of lunch. Perhaps a better plan would be quiet tables for people who want to read or rest. Surely that is fairer than a ban?

prompt.es: Según el segundo texto, ¿qué concede el autor antes de discrepar?

choices.text: That lunch is too short.
That teachers are unfair.
That phones can distract students in class.

feedback.es: «It is true that phones can distract us in class» es la concesión; después Nevertheless introduce su objeción.

origin.text: Many schools now ask students to leave their phones in a locker during lunch. In my view, this is a mistake. It is true that phones can distract us in class. A survey in one school found that students talked more when phones were allowed, which may suggest that the real problem is not the phone. Some teachers say that phones make the room quieter, but I wonder whether silence is really the goal of lunch. Perhaps a better plan would be quiet tables for people who want to read or rest. Surely that is fairer than a ban?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recurso de cautela usa la hablante.

choices.text: She limits her conclusion and admits the evidence is small.
She asks a rhetorical question to persuade.
She gives a strict order.

feedback.es: May suggest y more data would help limitan la conclusión: admite que la prueba no es definitiva.

origin.audio: The survey may suggest that students are happier outside, but more data would help.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Seguramente todos quieren una calle más segura?»

feedback.es: Surely abre una pregunta retórica que da por obvia la respuesta.

prompt.es: Lee el texto breve y elige el tono del autor.

choices.text: Happy and proud.
Disappointed but reasonable.
Sarcastic and cold.

feedback.es: Disappointed y Surely there is a fairer way? muestran decepción, pero el autor comprende al municipio: tono razonable.

origin.text: The new bus timetable starts next week. To be honest, I am disappointed. The buses will run less often, although the town is growing. The council says it must save money, and I understand that. Still, fewer buses will leave people stuck at home. Surely there is a fairer way?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la tesis de la hablante.

choices.text: Students should eat at school.
Cooking is too hard for teenagers.
Cooking should be taught in every school.

feedback.es: «Every school should teach cooking» es la tesis; lo demás la apoya.

origin.audio: In my opinion, every school should teach cooking. It is a life skill, and it may also help students eat better.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los críticos dicen que la nueva regla es demasiado estricta.»

feedback.es: Critics introduce a quienes se oponen a la idea; el autor suele citarlos para después responderles.

origin.text: ___ say that the new rule is too strict.
